:::{#exm-poisson-log-partition-mean}
#### The mean of the Poisson distribution from its log-partition function

<!-- no-figure: the example compares two numbers computed from the same data -->

In @exm-poisson-exponential-family,
the [statistic](sufficiency.qmd#def-statistic) is $\statf{\rvar} = \rvar$
and the log-partition function is $\logpartitionf{\natparam} = \expf{\natparam}$.
By @thm-log-partition-mean,

$$
\E{\Rvar}
= \E{\statf{\Rvar}}
= \dif{\logpartitionf{\natparam}}{\natparam}
= \expf{\natparam}.
$$

Since $\expf{\natparam} = \rate$,
we have $\E{\Rvar} = \rate$,
the [mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-expectation)
of the [Poisson distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson).

To check @thm-log-partition-mean on data,
we compute its two sides separately for the cyclone counts of @exm-poisson-exponential-family,
with $\rate$ set to the [sample mean](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample-mean).
The left side adds $\rvar \, \pdf\paren{\rvar ; \rate}$ over the counts from 0 to 100,
and the right side is a central difference of $\logpartitionf{\natparam}$ at $\natparam = \logf{\rate}$.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: poisson-log-partition-mean-r
#| code-fold: false
cyclones <- c(6, 5, 4, 6, 6, 3, 12, 7, 4, 2, 6, 7, 4)
rate <- mean(cyclones)
natural_parameter <- log(rate)

counts <- 0:100
weighted_masses <- counts * dpois(counts, rate)
mean_statistic <- sum(weighted_masses)

log_partition <- exp
step <- 1e-6
log_partition_up <- log_partition(natural_parameter + step)
log_partition_down <- log_partition(natural_parameter - step)
derivative <- (log_partition_up - log_partition_down) / (2 * step)

tibble::tibble(mean_statistic, derivative)
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: poisson-log-partition-mean-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import poisson

cyclones = np.array([6, 5, 4, 6, 6, 3, 12, 7, 4, 2, 6, 7, 4])
rate = cyclones.mean()
natural_parameter = np.log(rate)

counts = np.arange(0, 101)
mean_statistic = np.sum(counts * poisson.pmf(counts, rate))

log_partition = np.exp
step = 1e-6
log_partition_up = log_partition(natural_parameter + step)
log_partition_down = log_partition(natural_parameter - step)
derivative = (log_partition_up - log_partition_down) / (2 * step)

pd.DataFrame({"mean_statistic": [mean_statistic], "derivative": [derivative]})
```

:::

The two sides agree at `r round(mean_statistic, 3)`,
and differ by `r format(abs(mean_statistic - derivative), digits = 2)`.
That difference is numerical error.
:::
